text:
incident-bot: PAGE -> SRE oncall @maria_sre: elevated prefix cache miss rate and downstream latency spikes across us-west-2 between 14:03-14:13 UTC. auto-escalate P1. links: https://logs.redwood.internal/trace/abcdef :rotating_light:

maria_sre: I’m on it. seeing >40% miss rate on prefix 'user:ctx:' from the aggregated metric. starting triage — initiating live timeline.

jordan_infra: tagging in. any deploys around 14:00? I see a config roll at 13:58 for cache-invalidation service (deploy/ci-9873).

kevin_prod: customer-facing: a handful of high-throughput tenants reported latency >1.5s and some request retries. no 5xx spike yet. ticket count rising.

maria_sre: collecting logs -> `gcloud logging read "resource.type=container AND jsonPayload.component=cache-proxy AND timestamp>=\"2026-02-27T14:00:00Z\"" --limit 1000` (link above). dropping relevant snippets here:

jordan_infra: ```
14:02:07 cache-proxy INFO prefix=user:ctx: miss (key batch=128) hit_rate=0.12 ttl=42s
14:02:09 cache-proxy WARN invalidation propagated key=user:ctx: reason=deploy:ci-9873 request_id=0x1a2b3c
14:03:12 cache-proxy INFO rewarm-queue len=0 rewarm-worker=0
14:04:01 cache-proxy ERROR backend-throttle fallback=true backend_latency=920ms
```

maria_sre: timeline (so far):
- 13:58 UTC: cache-invalidation service deploy `ci-9873` (config change: aggressive invalidation window from 5m->0m)
- 14:01 UTC: small uptick in misses, hitting /route X from a few tenants
- 14:02-14:06 UTC: miss rate spikes to 35-45% for prefixes starting with `user:ctx:`
- 14:05 UTC: rewarm workers saturated (0 active) -> backlog growing
- 14:08 UTC: latency increases reported by prod; some retries seen

olivia_support: flagged top affected customers: acme-co (prod), sparrow-app (staging but high traffic), ~12 other small tenants. Acme opened sev ticket referencing slow responses.

kevin_prod: initial hypothesis: deploy removed a graceful invalidation window so we invalidated many keys simultaneously causing cold cache storm; rewarm workers either misconfigured or starved -> cascade to backend causing latency.

jordan_infra: supporting evidence: invalidation log shows thousands of keys invalidated in a single sweep, rewarm-queue shows 0 workers (config override applied in same deploy), and backend throttle lines at 14:04.

maria_sre: mitigation options considered:
1) rollback deploy `ci-9873` (fast, restores previous invalidation window)
2) increase rewarm concurrency and rate-limit invalidation (config patch)
3) enable cached-fallback-to-ttl (serve slightly stale values) as temporary bandaid

maria_sre: action: rolling back `ci-9873` now (command: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/cache-invalidation -n infra --to-revision=ci-9872`). will monitor metrics. @jordan_infra take rewarm-worker ops?

jordan_infra: acknowledged. scaling rewarm-workers from 0 -> 8 (`k scale deployment rewarm-workers --replicas=8 -n infra`) and enabling backpressure limiter.

incident-bot: DEPLOYMENT ACTION -> rollback triggered by maria_sre at 14:10 UTC (runbook ref: /runbooks/cache-invalidation/rollback).

maria_sre: post-rollback observations:
- 14:11 UTC: miss rate dropped to ~12%
- 14:13 UTC: backend latency trending down to baseline
- 14:14 UTC: ticket volume stabilizing; acme-co reporting improved responses

olivia_support: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~8% of requests across us-west-2 experienced >500ms extra latency; top 3 tenants accounted for ~60% of the impact window (14:02-14:12). No data loss.

kevin_prod: mitigation verdict: rollback + scale rewarm-workers resolved immediate impact. we should follow up with safer rollout (canary and staged TTL change), alert tuning (prefix hit-rate alert at 15% sustained), and rewarm capacity test.

jordan_infra: owner assigned for immediate RCA write-up: @jordan_infra will take primary, @maria_sre co-author, @kevin_prod will add customer timeline & communications. Opening issue: https://issues.redwood.internal/INC-3219

maria_sre: notes to include in RCA:
- root cause: aggressive invalidation config removed buffering window, causing mass invalidation + rewarm starvation (operator error in deploy manifest)
- contributing factors: missing canary gating on config change, rewarm-worker default scaled-to-zero in new manifest, insufficient alert thresholds on prefix-hitdrop
- short-term mitigations: rollback, scale rewarm-workers, enabled backpressure
- long-term actions: pre-deploy validation for invalidation sweeps, automated canary for config changes, rewarm capacity smoke test in CI, alert re-tuning

olivia_support: will send templated customer note and update ongoing tickets with timeline + mitigation.

maria_sre: follow-ups assigned and deadlines:
- Jordan: RCA draft by EOD (link to INC-3219)
- Maria: postmortem write + metrics graphs (prefix hit-rate, rewarm-queue, backend latency) by tomorrow 12:00 UTC
- Kevin: customer comms & credits proposal by tomorrow 09:00 UTC

jordan_infra: will attach log slices and k8s diffs to the issue. sample diff: ```
- name: rewarm-workers
  replicas: 0
+ name: rewarm-workers
  replicas: 8
```

maria_sre: bookmarking final note: no SLA breach expected (alerts hit but upstream 5xx not present), but operational impact was clear. create postmortem and mark P1 resolved once RCA links + customer comms done. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE -> status: mitigated (rollback + scale). owners: jordan_infra, maria_sre, kevin_prod. issue: INC-3219. next update in #postmortems once RCA published.
